title: A refused form keeps what was typed
assertion: Text, a select, a text area, a checkbox, a checkbox group, a radio, a date and a month keep the person's values after a refusal, and a valid default never replaces a refused value; a password and a one-time code are emptied, and a note under each says so, asking a locked account for nothing; the action's state carries no value the person typed; a dropped connection keeps every value but the secrets, says the save is not confirmed and which values to type again, and every later press sends the request key of the dropped press until one is saved, even after the page is read again, so nothing is saved twice; a request key used before reads "Already sent", never "Not done"; a page whose CSRF token or request key is out of date is read again in place, and a second press saves with the values intact; a page read again that shows another person signed in, or no one, clears a form that holds what was typed, says so and invites no press
noFileReason: The forms are refused in a browser harness with in-memory actions, and on synthetic sign-ins and practices the seed creates; no file.
